howto.name: Drop your PDF
howto.text: Select a PDF up to 500 MB that contains tables or tabular data. Scanned PDFs need OCR first via the OCR PDF tool.

howto.name: Choose pages to scan
howto.text: Pick specific pages with tables, or let the tool auto-detect tables across the whole document using Camelot and Tabula libraries.

howto.name: Tune detection (optional)
howto.text: For borderless or unusual tables, switch detection mode (lattice for ruled tables, stream for whitespace-separated). Default auto-selects the best.

howto.name: Convert and download
howto.text: Click Convert. Each detected table becomes a separate sheet in the resulting .xlsx file, with rows and columns preserved. Multiple tables across pages are combined into one workbook.

faq.q: Does it convert the entire PDF or just tables?
faq.a: The tool focuses on extracting tabular data. Each detected table becomes a separate sheet in the Excel file. Non-table text (paragraphs, headers, footers) is not included — use PDF to Word or PDF to Text for that.

faq.q: Can I choose which tables to extract?
faq.a: Yes. Select specific pages, or let the tool auto-detect all tables across the document. Auto-detect uses Camelot and Tabula libraries which identify ruled lines and text-alignment patterns.

faq.q: What if my PDF has no visible table borders?
faq.a: The tool can detect tables based on text alignment even without ruled borders, but results are more reliable on clearly bordered tables. For borderless tables with very irregular spacing, manual page selection plus column-position hints in the advanced settings give better accuracy.

faq.q: What happens to a confidential financial PDF after I upload it?
faq.a: The PDF is uploaded over HTTPS and converted in isolated temporary per-request storage on the PrivaTools server, using local libraries rather than a third-party API. Response cleanup removes the PDF and the generated .xlsx after the result is sent, and a background sweep clears anything left behind by an interrupted request.

Up to 500 MB per file on the hosted site. Table extraction is one of the heavier jobs, so fair-use rate limits apply and a very long PDF can hit the request timeout; splitting the document first avoids that.

faq.q: Does it work on scanned PDFs?
faq.a: Scanned PDFs need OCR first. Run the OCR PDF tool (you can pick the language and deskew the pages), then convert the OCR'd PDF to Excel. The text layer added by OCR is what the table detector reads.

faq.q: Can I batch-convert multiple PDFs to Excel?
faq.a: Yes — upload multiple PDFs and each is converted independently, then bundled into a ZIP of .xlsx files. Useful for processing a folder of monthly statements or invoices.

Tables with clear ruled lines and one value per cell. Merged cells, tables that break across pages and borderless layouts with irregular spacing are the hardest cases and usually need tidying in the spreadsheet afterwards.
